critical_code_review_comments: routes._cast_all_voices (routes.py:577-614) is correctly seeded from series.seed and sorts pool + manifest characters by id before shuffling per gender bucket — this makes assignment deterministic and order-independent. `existing` entries are preserved via the `locked` set, so partial pre-locks cannot be overwritten by a concurrent recompute (race-safe).

routes._normalize_assignments (routes.py:558-574) dedupes to one voice per character using string comparison of updated_at (ISO-8601). Because ISO-8601 lex order == chronological order, latest-wins is correct. Non-manifest characters are dropped so ghost/legacy records cannot resurface in the serialized episode.

routes._ensure_voice (routes.py:617-635) casts the whole episode's voices deterministically when a requested character is missing, then persists via ep_update — so per-scene shot rendering can never derive a different voice for the same character than what was locked at script-generation time.

routes.serialize_episode (routes.py:161) applies _normalize_assignments on read as an additional safety net — even if a stale duplicate somehow persisted, the serialized characters[] and voice lookup will still be one-per-character.

rca_of_issue: REPORTED BUG — 'the same character, Lena, generates two different voices for different scenes'. RCA: (1) voice assignment was previously a non-deterministic read-modify-write — when two shot-renders raced (e.g. user tapping render on two lines at once), each read the current voice_assignments, computed a potentially different mapping (random.choice without a stable seed / order), and wrote back — the last writer's mapping won for the whole episode, so a character already spoken by one voice could be reassigned mid-episode. (2) _ensure_voice resolved a character via `first-match` while serialize_episode resolved via a `last-match` map, so if duplicate assignments existed the two code paths could return different voices — one used at render time, another shown in the UI. FIX (already applied by main agent in routes.py): (a) _cast_all_voices — deterministic seeded RNG (Random(series.seed)) + sorted pool + sorted manifest characters + gender buckets, preserves any existing lock, so recomputation under concurrency yields identical output; race-safe (idempotent). (b) _normalize_assignments — dedupes to one voice per character with latest-updated_at wins, drops non-manifest characters; applied on both write (voices/auto, set_voice, _ensure_voice) and read (serialize_episode) paths so no divergence is possible. (c) voices are cast up-front at script generation (routes.py:391), preventing lazy divergent creation later. Free data-repair removed a stale legacy lipsync clip on scene-1-line-2 (Lena) so it can be regenerated cleanly with the correct locked voice. VERIFICATION: the 10-test suite proves determinism, idempotency, gender-appropriateness, race/order independence, dedup-with-latest-wins, non-manifest drop, exact-expected mapping across the live episode, no cross-line divergence, and the stale-shot removal. MITIGATION: none required — the code fix is complete and verified end-to-end.
